items.title: The Department of Justice Is Using AI Detector Pangram Against Defense Attorneys
items.excerpt: Federal prosecutors are running defense filings through the Pangram AI-text detector and citing the results in court, extending AI-writing detection from publishing and classrooms into litigation.
items.rationale: New, original reporting: the AI-writing detector that publishers and prize juries rely on is now being cited by federal prosecutors in court, which raises the stakes of false positives for anyone who writes.

items.title: Over 500 million Claude tokens help explain 1,000 years of Persian poetry
items.excerpt: Toronto engineer Arman Nejad used Claude to write modern-Persian explanations for more than 1.6 million couplets by all 245 poets in the Ganjoor archive, from Rudaki to Shahriar, now live on Ganjoor and in its public data repo.
items.rationale: A concrete, shipped release: LLM-written commentary on a whole literary canon, now live in Ganjoor's archive and public data repo. It is a model for AI-assisted annotation of classic texts.

items.title: Wizards of the Coast shares AI copyright settlement money with D&D's authors
items.excerpt: Wizards of the Coast, which filed Bartz v. Anthropic claims as copyright owner of D&D novels and modules, says it will pass its share of the $1.5bn settlement (about $3,000 per book) to the writers who created those works.
items.rationale: A new decision by a rights-holding publisher: it will route its Anthropic settlement payouts to the work-for-hire writers. This sets a precedent for how publishers split AI-training money with creators.

items.title: 비플릭스, AI 기술로 웹툰에 움직임 더한 '무빙툰' 출시
items.excerpt: 국내 OTT 비플릭스가 AI로 정지된 웹툰 컷마다 움직임을 입힌 '무빙툰' 서비스를 모바일·PC 웹에 출시했다. 다른 웹툰 서비스에도 적용 가능한 기술이라고 밝혔다.
items.rationale: A fresh product launch: AI adds motion to each static webtoon panel, and the company says the technology can be licensed to other webtoon services. This is a new reading format for comics IP.

items.title: Cambridge Dictionary names 'human' Word of the Year 2026
items.excerpt: Cambridge Dictionary picked 'human' as its 2026 Word of the Year for a year 'defined by global debates on what it means to be human when AI is blurring the boundaries between people and machines'.
items.rationale: An official announcement from a major reference publisher, reported by an on-whitelist trade outlet. AI is the stated reason for the choice, and it reflects the 'human-made' push running through publishing this year.

https://www.wargamer.com/dnd/anthropic-s.new_action: Wizards of the Coast announced it will pass its Bartz v. Anthropic settlement share (~$3,000 per book) to the D&D writers who created the works. This is a new decision by a new party, not settlement-claim logistics.
